title: Bessarabia
capsule: Bessarabia was annexed by the Russian Empire following the Russo-Turkish War of 1806–1812 and formally ceded by the Ottoman Empire under the Treaty of Bucharest signed on 28 May 1812, making it a Russian oblast between the Prut and Dniester rivers and the Black Sea coast. The region had been part of the Moldavian principality for most of its history and retained a predominantly Romanian-speaking Orthodox Christian population under Russian rule. The from/to dates of 1812–1814 in this dataset reflect the earliest administrative phase before the oblast was reorganized; Russia held the bulk of the territory until 1918, when it united with Romania following the Russian Revolution.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The treaty boundaries of 1812 Bessarabia are precisely defined by the Prut and Dniester rivers, but the 1812–1814 window in this dataset captures only the initial military occupation phase before formal administrative organization, making the exact polygon somewhat approximate.
